baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Rodgers builds on Wiebe’s account of organizational change while treating bureaucratic social efficiency as one progressive language among several.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Own1982 historiographical essay,117–118 and127/n59, praises the link between organizational transformation and one strand of thought while explicitly noting that Wiebe had already made qualifications that later inquiries swamped. This specified resource coexists with Rodgers’s criticism of simplification; it does not make Wiebe responsible for Rodgers’s entire three-language interpretation. The Search for Order and later1973 essay remain unread here.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Rodgers argues that Wiebe’s organizational synthesis simplified progressive ideas and left the relation between professionalization and social visions insufficiently explained.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Own1982 essay,118–119, qualifies the new-middle-class carrier thesis and distinguishes job control from a shared bureaucratic political ethos. He praises Wiebe’s account of organizational change and later credits his earlier qualifications,n59; this is not a wholesale rejection. Hays’s more sweeping functionalist explanation is a separate target and is not silently assigned to Wiebe.
